newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque radical newspaper editor denies aiding ETA.
newsitem.headline: Basque radical newspaper editor denies aiding ETA.

text.p: The editor of a radical Basque newspaper went on trial in Madrid on Monday and denied charges that he had supplied information to the separatist guerrilla group ETA.

Jose Benigno Rei, editor of Egin, accused the Basque government of mounting a smear campaign against him and said he had been branded an ETA collaborator because of "personal animosity" harboured by Basque Interior Minister Juan Maria Atutxa.
Rei is accused of providing financial and other information on companies to ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) which could later have been used for extortion, kidnapping or murder.
Basque businessmen have long complained of intimidation by ETA, saying they receive threatening letters to demand payment of a "revolutionary tax".
Rei said any of a number of journalists or Egin employees had access to the information in question which was kept in unlocked cabinets.

Rei was arrested after police found papers, including a list of potential ETA targets, in Egin's offices in December 1994. A similar list was alleged to have been found on a suspected ETA leader arrested months earlier.
If convicted, Rei could face up to eight years in prison.
His case attracted international attention and he has won support from prominent U.S. educator and linguist Noam Chomsky, a longtime supporter of Amnesty International and other rights groups.
Egin usually publishes ETA communiques and is seen as a mouthpiece for the rebel group which has killed about 800 people in a drive for independence begun in 1968.
